reviews.title: Beware of the BRICK plug
reviews.review_text: Product works great for my iPhone 13 and Series 7 watch to charge them. I knocked off 1 star, maybe should have done 2, because of the BRICK plug that is on the plug end that goes into the wall. Why not build that into the base? The brick plug does block my USB plugs and my 2 plug, which is major design flub.

reviews.title: Mixed feelings
reviews.review_text: The products are fine. I get a least an email a day asking to buy more. I unsubscribe every time I get one and they keep coming. I don't respect or purchase from vendors that ignore my requests, and therer are lots of these types of products on the market but I do enjoy my product from belkin

reviews.title: A more camera bump friendly charger
reviews.review_text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Ordered this for my wife, to replace another charger she was using. The old one was wireless, but not MagSafe, and once we upgraded to the iPhone 14 Pro with it's more prominent camera bump, it was lifted too high to charge. We chose this Belkin Charger because of it's slightly elevated MagSafe charger built in. so far she really likes it.

reviews.title: Aligning the phone to charge is a pain
reviews.review_text: After travelling 2 months with it, heres my honest feedback: Works well with the watch and pods. But not with the charging pad for the iPhone 13... To be clear. The wireless charging pad works. But aligning my phone can be tricky and misleading. It was not what I imagine where u can just drop the phone on the surface and expect it to charge. You have to position the phone on top of the pad until u hear a ding and see the lighting symbol showing on ur phone. Sound easy right? I thought so when I watch the YouTube reviews. It sometimes takes a few tries to get the alignment right. And when there's the ding sound and lighting sign on the phone screen, I had to wait for sign to go off and check and make sure the phone is charging. The reason to check is because the sounds and signs only tells you it detect the alignment, but it does not confirms it is charging. The last time I did the above, let my 10% batt phone charge overnight, woke up found my phone still 10%. It could be accidentally bump the table/charger and cause to misalign the phone and charge pad. Or anything else. But after that, I just went back using my lightning cable. Conclusion. For people who got the money, loves the wireless concept and don't mind the above issue, go for it. For people on a budget and/or focus more on practicalities and efficiencies, just stick with the cable for the phones and original chargers for the pods and watches.

reviews.title: Uneven charging performance
reviews.review_text: I've been using this for a couple of months to charge my iPhone12Pro, AirPodsPro, and AppleWatch 7. It charges the earbuds & watch just fine, but half the time it drains the battery on the phone even though I don't use a case, no matter how properly I position it on the disc. Sometimes it charges, but other times it drains the battery. (I keep the phone on the pad at bedside, as it is not the iPhone I use for anything other than an alarm clock or music). All my connections are firm--otherwise the earbuds & watch wouldn't charge.

reviews.title: Much heavier than expected: 1 pound
reviews.review_text: Works fine. Much heavier than expected: 1 pound+ Bought this for travel so 1 pound is more than I want, especially when I can get other charging pads that are 10oz.

reviews.title: Not charging the iPhone XS Max
reviews.review_text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I bought the charging pod from Apple. It says that my iPhone XS Max and Apple Watch series 4 are compatible with this product. I put the iPhone on the charging pod (at at least 90%) and it did say that it was charging. In the morning, the iPhone battery was at 87%. That's when I understood the iPhone wasn't charging at all. Really disappointed.
